item.title: Spark Program | ShareCut: referral payouts for small shops over Fiber (testnet) (1 posts)
item.description: 1. Project Overview Small shops in Lagos get most new customers by word of mouth, but they rarely track it or pay the people who bring customers in. ShareCut gives each promoter a personal link or QR code. When a customer they referred pays through Fiber, the promoter’s agreed cut is paid automatically and both payments appear on a public receipts page. ShareCut builds on an existing Fiber checkout and adds three things: referral attribution, an automatic payout service, and public receipts. It runs on testnet only, takes 6 weeks, and ends with a pilot in at least 2 real shops. 2. Team Profile Name: Abdul (solo applicant) Location: Lagos, Nigeria (student at the University of Lagos)...

item.title: A second post-quantum lock for CKB? ML-DSA beside SPHINCS+, checked and measured (1 posts)
item.description: What each signature rests on, and what that safety costs1600×900 80.3 KB This is a study and a prototype, on testnet only, with code that is days old. In short CKB has one lock today built to resist a quantum computer: SPHINCS+. We built a second one, on ML-DSA, another finished NIST standard. At the same security level it costs about a third as much on chain, and it signs in milliseconds where SPHINCS+ takes about a second. The price is trust: ML-DSA leans on newer maths than SPHINCS+. It is not safer, and SPHINCS+ stays the careful choice for savings. We are asking two things: try to break it, and tell us whether CKB wants a second lock at all.
